ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within the Cartesian coordinate system, the quadrilateral \(OABC\) is a square. Point \(B\) has the coordinates \((2\sqrt{2}, 0)\). Point \(D\) is a moving point on ray \(OB\) that does not coincide with point \(O\). Segment \(CD\) is rotated \(90^\circ\) clockwise around point \(D\) to obtain \(ED\), and segments \(AD\) and \(AE\) are drawn. \(DA=DE\); As in figure 2, by connecting \(AC\) and \(BE\), when triangles \(CDA\) and \(DBE\) are similar, what is the length of \(BD\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in Figure 2, let AC intersect OB at point J, and draw DK $\perp$ BC at point K. \\
$\because$ DA=DC=DE, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$DAC=$\angle$DCA, $\angle$DAE=$\angle$DEA, \\
$\because$ $\triangle ADC$ is similar to $\triangle EBD$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ACD=$\angle$DEB, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$CAD=$\angle$DAE, \\
$\because$ $\angle$CAB=$\angle$ACB=$45^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$CAD=$\angle$DAB=$\angle$ACD=$\angle$BCD=$22.5^\circ$, \\
$\because$ DJ$\perp$CJ, DK$\perp$CB, \\
$\therefore$ DJ=DK, \\
$\because$ B$(2\sqrt{2},0)$, \\
$\therefore$ OJ=JB=$\sqrt{2}$, \\
$\therefore$ DJ+$\sqrt{2}$DJ=$\sqrt{2}$, \\
$\therefore$ DJ=$2-\sqrt{2}$, \\
$\therefore$ OD=2, \\
$\therefore$ BD=$2\sqrt{2}-2$; \\
Therefore, the length of BD is $BD=\boxed{2\sqrt{2}-2}$.
